# The provenance file on Sšꜣt

*The provenance file for Sšꜣt. Nothing here is unsourced; that is what the file is for.*

## Provenance

**1. The attestation.** **𓋇𓏏𓁐**, from the tradition's own record. On record: Seti I temple, Abydos: foundation reliefs (Dynasty 19), Temple of Edfu: Ptolemaic foundation texts, Palermo Stone (royal annals, Dynasty 5), Lexikon der Ägyptologie, s.v. 'Seshat'.

**2. The narrative record.** **Pedj-Shes** — The pedj-shes, ‘stretching of the cord’, opens every temple: at night, sighting on the stars, the king and Sšꜣt stretch a cord between stakes to fix the building’s axis — she the goddess of measurement, he the builder under her hand.  The reliefs show the rite exactly and never change it: Seti I’s temple at Abydos (Dynasty 19), Hatshepsut’s foundation works, and the Ptolemaic temples of Edfu and Dendera a thousand years later all show the same two figures facing each other, mallet and pole in hand, the captions declaiming the grip on peg and cord. **The Notches of Time** — At the jubilee, the sed-festival, she offers the king the palm-rib notched with countless years — ‘I give you years as numerous as those of Ra. ’ She is the accountant of eternity: regnal years, the biennial cattle-census, the flood’s height, the captured spoil — all are inscribed by her.

**3. The physical record.** Her iconography is remarkably consistent across three millennia: leopard-skin robe, seven-pointed emblem on a double horizontal bar, palm-rib in hand. The finest foundation reliefs — Seti I at Abydos, Hatshepsut's foundation deposits, Edfu and Dendera's Ptolemaic versions — show the cord-stretching in identical form, a ritual grammar unchanged from Old Kingdom to Rome. Foundation deposits under real temples (model tools, plaques, the cord's physical traces) confirm the rite was performed, not just pictured.

**4. The current holding.** The temple at [/seshat/](/seshat/), classified Tier 1. Tier-1 is not a compliment; it is a measurement. This restoration keeps something the ASCII form provably loses, and the measurement is repeatable.

**5. The documented resonances.** **Education, Research & Knowledge**, **Writing, Publishing & Media**, **Software, Cloud & Developer Infrastructure** — seats argued and weighted in the [pattern atlas](/patterns/), read through the myths in this temple's [Resonance File](/seshat/blog/resonance/).

**6. The primary sources.** [The Book of the Dead](/texts/book-of-the-dead/) — the library this file answers to, open at the [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/).

**7. The continuing record.** She embodies an idea the modern world runs on: that power follows from record — the survey, the ledger, the archive.  Egyptologists cite her rite in every study of temple alignment (the "stretching of the cord" is the founding document of archaeoastronomy), and her palm-rib is the ancestor of every tally, census, and database.
